author: Michael Garcia
title: SFA asks court to halt order preserving women's sports teams - NewsBreak
text: NACOGDOCHES, Texas ( KETK ) – Stephen F. Austin State University has asked the United States District Court for the Eastern of Texas to stay an order that would force the school to maintain several women’s sports teams. On Aug. 1, the court issued a preliminary injunction against SFA that ordered the university to maintain their varsity women’s beach volleyball team, the Ladyjacks bowling team, and the men’s and women’s golf teams, after they cut the programs earlier this year . The order comes as several women athletes have filed a lawsuit against SFA alleging that the school violated Title IX by cutting the teams. The university appealed the order on Monday, citing the financial and logistical difficulties they say they’d face by maintaining the sports teams. “Testimony over the course of the two-day preliminary injunction hearing revealed that it would be financially significant and logistically improbable for SFA to reinstate three teams with such a limited deadline until the start of the Fall semester,” SFA’s motion for a stay against the order said. The university claimed that there aren’t enough student athletes to fill out the minimum roster needed for the women’s beach volleyball, women’s golf and women’s bowling teams ahead of the start of the fall semester on Aug. 25. “In fact, much of Plaintiffs’ argument was that the teams could eventually be fielded for the spring semester,” SFA claimed. “Their own expert even posited that it could take three to four years to reinstate the teams. Despite this testimony, however, the trial court improperly assigned more weight to the athletes (who are not athletics administrators) and two of the three coaches that the teams could be fielded.” SFA added that on top of recruiting athletes, they’d also have to find coaches for the beach volleyball and women’s golf. SFA said they’d also have to schedule games, competitions, facilities and travel for all the teams. SFA Athletic Director Michael McBroom reportedly testified that it would take around $1 million to reinstate the teams at issue in the lawsuit, according to SFA’s appeal. KETK News spoke with the lead counsel for the women athletes, Arthur Bryant, on Wednesday. He explained that SFA could have to wait awhile to have their appeal heard by a higher court so they’re asking the local federal district court Judge Michael J. Truncale to rule on their motion to stay his own order by Thursday. SFA’s motion says that if Truncale doesn’t rule on the motion by Thursday they’ll appeal his injunction to the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals in New Orleans. “SFA has made it clear in what they filed with the judge, the motion for a stay, that if he does not rule very quickly on it, they intend to go to the appeals court and ask them to rule on it, even though he hasn’t had much time to even consider it,” Bryant said. Bryant argues that the plaintiffs haven’t even had much time to respond to SFA’s motion before Thursday either. “Of course, we haven’t had a chance to even respond to it yet,” Bryant said. “So SFA is doing what it can to try to eliminate these teams in violation of Title IX and speed up the whole process so it can do it as quickly as possible.” Ultimately, Bryant says SFA shouldn’t have put saving money over the rights of their athletes. “It made a conscious decision to violate Title IX, basically for money, and you can’t discriminate against people to save money,” Bryant said. “It’s going to be held accountable and it ought to just comply with the law.” Court records show that Judge Truncale hasn’t responded to SFA’s motion for a stay as of Wednesday night.
